Configuration sections and WAF protection areas

Live browsers for every FortiWeb configuration section — the WAF protection areas (API Protection, Bot Mitigation, DoS and more) and the System, Network, User & Authentication and Log & Report menus — each with its own config-template library.

👤 ForOperatorAdministrator
🔑 Permissionsnetwork.edit protection.edit operations.template_save operations.template_apply users.manage
📍 WhereFortiWeb ADOM, no sidebar entry since 3.1.0: the same objects are on FortiWeb's own pages under FortiWeb → <group> → <page> (URL /configuration/ and /configuration/<section_key>; ?type=<object type> redirects to the measured page unless ?classic=1)

What is it?#

FortiWeb groups its configuration into GUI sections. SATOM gives each section a live browser: a menu that mirrors the FortiWeb menu, an object list for the selected type on the selected device, and the shared object editor opening inline under the row. Each page also keeps a config template library for the selected object type, so a configuration can be captured once and pushed to other devices.

Since SATOM 3.1.0 the sidebar no longer draws these sections. The FortiWeb device menu — FortiWeb's own GUI menu, measured on the device's build — draws the same objects on pages in FortiWeb's layout (for example FortiWeb → API Protection → JSON Protection or FortiWeb → System → Config → SNMP), and those pages carry the same config template library (see Server Objects for how they work). The section pages described here still open by URL.

What does it do?#

  • WAF protection areas. Seven sections, each a collapsible copy of the FortiWeb menu: Application Delivery, API Protection, Bot Mitigation, DoS Protection, IP Protection, Machine Learning and Tracking. Each menu entry opens a page whose tabs are the object types of that entry. Until 3.1.0 they formed the sidebar WAF group.
  • Configuration sections. The remaining sections that have a curated menu — System, Network, User & Authentication and Log & Report — as section → group → object type trees. Until 3.1.0 they formed the sidebar Configuration group.
  • All sections page (/configuration/, reached from the Configuration breadcrumb or the All sections button) shows every section as a card with its number of object types and badges: live browser, danger (Network) and read-only (Dashboard / Monitor).
  • On a section page, appends an Other Objects group listing every other configuration object the registry files under the section, so nothing the device has is hidden.
  • Lists objects from SATOM's local copy, with a freshness badge and Refresh from device.
  • Edits objects inline (Edit opens the editor under the row; Close closes it), creates them with New and deletes them with a two-step dry-run confirmation.
  • Detects single-configuration objects (global settings, DNS, NTP…) and edits them as one object, labelled single config.
  • For file-backed objects (schemas, WSDL, DTD…), replaces New with New and Stored copies (see WAF artifacts).
  • Keeps a Config template library per object type: New template, View, Apply to devices, Clone, Delete, and Save as template from an open object.
  • Sections without a curated menu (Dashboard / Monitor) show a read-only Object types catalogue (Logical, URN, Singleton, Danger) instead.

The FortiWeb Sections page (Section Catalog) is the opposite view: it lists only approved templates, grouped by section, for use in System Provisioning.

Requirements#

  • A FortiWeb device selected as the current device. Section pages always work on that device. Without one, section pages redirect to the Architecture page.
  • A local copy of the device configuration (use Refresh from device on a device never synchronised).

Permissions#

Every page under /configuration/ — including the WAF protection areas and Refresh from device — requires configuration-write permission. Any of network.edit, network.apply, protection.edit, protection.apply, operations.apply, operations.template_save, operations.template_apply, operations.template_approve, appliances.edit or appliances.apply grants it.

Action Required
Open any section page, refresh, edit objects Configuration write (see above)
Save as template, New template, Clone, Delete template operations.template_save
Apply to devices — one device operations.template_apply
Apply to devices — several devices operations.template_apply and operations.apply, and the template must be approved
FortiWeb Sections (Section Catalog) users.manage (Administrator)

🔑Permission — What users without permission see

Every section page returns the 403 page to users without configuration-write permission. Save as template appears only if you hold operations.template_save; the other template buttons are always displayed and are refused with 403 when you lack the permission. Save as template is also hidden on read-only (predefined) types.

ℹ️Note

Changed in 2.11.0: the WAF protection-area menus are now shown only to users who can open them (configuration-write permission).

ℹ️Note

Changed in 3.1.0: the FortiWeb ADOM no longer draws the WAF and Configuration sidebar groups, nor a Classic view button. The objects are on the pages of the FortiWeb device menu (FortiWeb → <group> → <page>). A section page link with ?type=<object type> redirects to the measured page that draws that collection; ?classic=1 keeps the section page. A collection that no measured page draws has no menu entry until its page is measured, and its section page still opens by URL.

How to use#

Browse and edit a section#

  1. Select a FortiWeb device.
  2. Open /configuration/ (All sections) and click a section card, or open /configuration/<section_key> directly (for example /configuration/system). The page opens on the first object type that has objects on this device. A menu entry whose collection a measured FortiWeb page draws takes you to that page; add ?classic=1 to the address to stay on the section page.
  3. Switch object types with the tabs above the list.
  4. Click Edit on a row: the editor opens under the row. Make changes and use Review & save → Apply to device, exactly as in the object editor.
  5. Click New to create, or the trash button to delete (preview first, then Apply this delete to the device now?).

⚠️Warning — Network section

The Network section shows Network-impacting section. Objects there (interfaces, routes, HA, admin) can cut management connectivity or split a cluster. Preview and test on one device first.

Refresh the local copy#

Click Refresh from device. The flash message reads Refreshed from <device>: <detail> (or Refresh failed: …).

Capture an object as a template#

  1. Open an object with Edit.
  2. Click Save as template in the editor header.
  3. Enter Template name and an optional Note, then Save template.
  4. The message Saved <name> (vN, M item(s)) — pending approval. confirms it. The template captures the object and its sub-table rows; it is never applied by this step.

Author, apply, clone or delete a template#

  • New template opens New
    template with Name, Note, Body (JSON) and Exceptions (JSON); Save Template stores it.
  • Apply to devices opens the apply dialog: select Target devices, click Dry-run preview, then Confirm live apply. See Template library.
  • Clone copies the template as <name> (copy); Delete asks Delete template '<name>' (vN)? This cannot be undone.

The library on each page shows templates captured from the selected object type, plus authored templates that do not name an object type.

Review approved templates (administrators)#

  1. Open Template Library and click FortiWeb Sections.
  2. Approved templates are grouped by section (Web Protection, Server Policy, System, Structure, then each configuration section).
  3. View opens the template as JSON; Revoke returns it to pending.

Configuration#

Save-as-template dialog:

Field Description Required Example
Template name Name in the library. Saving an existing name creates the next version. Yes baseline-system
Note Free text shown in the library. No NTP and DNS for branch sites

Example#

🧪Example — Reuse a bot-mitigation policy

  1. On fweb-01, open FortiWeb → Bot Mitigation → Bot Mitigation Policy.
  2. Select bot-shop, click Save as template and name it bot-baseline.
  3. An administrator approves bot-baseline in the Template library.
  4. Back on the same page, in the config template library under the table, Apply to devices → select fweb-02 and fweb-03 → Dry-run preview → Confirm live apply.

Result#

  • Object edits are written and audited as described in Object editor.
  • A saved template lands pending in the Template library under the kind config:<section>.
  • A confirmed apply runs as a background job in the job dock.

Troubleshooting#

The page shows the 403 error#

Possible causes - You do not hold configuration-write permission (this applies to the WAF protection areas too). The sidebar hides these entries from you, so the page was opened from a bookmark or a shared link.

Solution 1. Ask an administrator for protection.edit or network.edit.

"Pick an object type from the sidebar menu"#

The section has a menu but no type is selected. Choose an entry in the sidebar.

The badge says "no local data — refresh"#

Click Refresh from device. On a device never synchronised at all, the list is read live once.

"A template name is required."#

Enter a Template name in the Save as template dialog.

"object not found on device" or "device read failed: …"#

Possible causes - Save as template reads the object live; the object was deleted or the device is unreachable.

Solution 1. Refresh, check the device, and try again.

"unknown section" / "endpoint not allowed"#

The request named a section or collection SATOM does not know; reopen the page from the sidebar.

Advanced#

Advanced Menus and gating

Curated menus come from SATOM (GUI-faithful groups and labels) and are resolved against the endpoint registry, so types the firmware does not ship are dropped. The sidebar hides types that the appliance's feature visibility disables; the section page still serves them. Sub-table rows never appear as menu entries — they are edited inside their parent object.

Advanced Template body

A captured template is a root node with no endpoint whose subobjects are the object first (create, or update for a single-configuration object) and then one create per sub-table row, with ids and read-only keys removed so the body applies cleanly to another device.
